📖 How to use

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is modular arithmetic?

Modular arithmetic is arithmetic with a “wrap-around” modulus m: results are always reduced to the range 0…m−1, like hours on a 12-hour clock.

How is a^b mod m computed for large b?

With square-and-multiply (binary exponentiation), which needs only O(log b) multiplications instead of b multiplications, so even huge exponents finish instantly.

When does a modular inverse exist?

a⁻¹ mod m exists exactly when gcd(a, m) = 1, i.e. a and m are coprime. The tool uses the extended Euclidean algorithm and tells you when no inverse exists.
